clue.text: River quietens with injection of hydrogen

blocks.note: to tame something is to subdue or quieten it

explanation.walkthrough: The H goes in after the first letter of TAMES to give London's river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames is the famous river flowing through London, so it is a straightforward example of the category named.

clue.text: Price rise beginning to rile rambler

blocks.note: a hike is an increase in a price or rate
the opening letter of this word

explanation.walkthrough: 'Price rise' reads as a cause of annoyance, but it is simply a noun meaning a sharp increase.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler is someone who walks the countryside for pleasure, exactly the same activity as one who goes walking on trails.

clue.text: Little risk for speaker in a quick meal

explanation.definitionFit: A minute steak is a thin cut of beef fried very briefly, so it makes a fast dinner.

clue.text: Vessel more readily allowing first couple of children on board

the first couple of a word's letters are its opening two, so only those are kept

the opening two letters of this word

explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' finishes the nautical picture and doubles as the placing of the two letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing ship with two or more masts, so it is a kind of seagoing vessel.

clue.text: Gosh! Pound will get a good picnic accessory

L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra
to bag something is to get or secure it

explanation.surface: An excited shopper exclaims that a pound will buy something handy for a picnic.

explanation.definitionFit: An insulated bag keeps food and drinks chilled outdoors, which makes it useful on an outing to eat in the open air.

clue.text: Family spook finally producing sound of chains?

the closing letter of this word

explanation.walkthrough: The ghost story is nearly all scene-setting; only the last letter of 'spook' is used.

clue.text: Gutted contralto picked up items on score, but not opening sequences of notes

blocks.note: the outer letters of this word
a musical score is written on staves, the sets of five lines

explanation.definitionFit: An octave is a series of eight notes running from one pitch to the next of the same name, so a scale span.

about means around, so one piece is wrapped round another
a probe goes inside something, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: GB stands for Great Britain
rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

Co is the abbreviation for company
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Braggadocio is boastful, arrogant talk, the same empty swagger that bluster describes.

clue.text: Leave and spot someone expected to appear?

blocks.note: to go is to leave
a dot is a small spot

explanation.surface: Someone leaves and then notices a person who is supposed to turn up.

clue.text: Confident males, modest, relinquishing power

clue.text: Poor justification to produce firewood, say, before a lot of cold weather

clue.text: It’s hard to carry, making you grumpy

clue.text: Slow-moving vehicle covering each mile with walker

clue.text: Unhappy end darkens this cartoon film
